title: tenant-aware-auth-and-cors-preflight-normalization
author: Leah Kim
description: Motivation: Reduce ambiguity between org- and project-scoped credentials and make CORS preflight semantics deterministic across hosted and private installs. This PR introduces a tenant-aware Authorization negotiation layer plus a small header versioning handshake to let clients opt into the new behavior gradually. It also normalizes CORS preflight responses for the streaming endpoints and separates the streaming reconnect token from the primary auth header to avoid accidental credential leakage during long-lived WS/stream reconnects. Key user-facing changes: 1) New optional header X-Redwood-Auth-Version (v=1|v=2). When present, the server will apply tenant-aware resolution (project keys, org keys, tenant tokens) and return structured warning hints in the WWW-Authenticate payload to assist SDKs in selecting the correct key scope. 2) Authorization header mapping: we accept the legacy OpenAI-compatible Bearer token but will emit a Deprecation-Warning response header when the token can be disambiguated as an org-level key while a project-scoped token is required. 3) New X-Redwood-Stream-Connect header for reconnect handshakes; this header accepts short-lived tokens produced by the streaming gateway to avoid replaying long-lived credentials. 4) Tool/function-call signatures: requests that route to server-side tool-call handlers must include X-Redwood-Signature and X-Redwood-Signature-KeyId. The signing format is HMAC-SHA256 over the canonicalized tool payload; the SDKs are updated to produce signatures transparently. 5) CORS: preflight responses for streaming and REST endpoints now include a deterministic Vary: Origin and expose headers list that contains X-Redwood-Stream-Connect and X-Redwood-Auth-Version to aid browsers performing preflight checks. Backwards compatibility: Default behavior is unchanged for clients that do not send X-Redwood-Auth-Version and for installs without tenant routing enabled. Migration path: - [x] Add X-Redwood-Auth-Version support to SDKs (TS/Python/Go) with transparent fallthrough. - [x] Canary tenant-aware routing on Dedicated in eu-west-1 for 2 weeks. - [x] Emit Deprecation-Warning header for ambiguous tokens (non-blocking). - [x] Docs and migration guide added under docs/api/auth.md. Rollout notes: start in canary, monitor auth-error-rate and streaming-reconnect-rate metrics in Console. If error spike > 1% above baseline for 1 hour, rollback tenant routing. Security: signing keys are rotated using existing KMS integration; no plaintext keys logged. Testing: unit coverage added for header parsing, integration test for browser preflight and streaming reconnect. See linked Linear items for acceptance criteria and rollout checklist.
